title: Choose skillet's dark world
question: The roll assigned The Tasting Menu. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Tasting Menu
options.lineage: fine-dining tasting menus, low-lit dining rooms
options.thesis: Your five next skills served as a five-course tasting menu, each salary effect set in the price column.
materials: brass reserved for the five courses
options.viewport: Left rail holds the profile and stack controls; the main column is the menu card: five numbered courses (I-V), each skill name, an italic evidence note, dot leaders to a right-aligned salary effect, and the prix-fixe total (+82%, 95% CI +72% to +92%) closing the card.
options.risk: The food metaphor can turn twee if pushed past type, palette and the price column; a 'price' can be misread as a cost unless the column is labelled 'salary effect'.

raised.raise: Brass is reserved for one job: it marks only the five recommended skills, wherever they appear (menu, chart, calculator).
The menu and the chart share one index: course numerals I-V reappear on the ROI chart bars and in the calculator.
Density courage: every course carries its full evidence (effect, p, n, peers who know it, peers who want it, 95% CI) in one tabular line, no padded tiles.

options.label: The Star Atlas
options.lineage: celestial star atlases; also dealt by the catalog as a challenger
options.thesis: Your stack drawn as a constellation in skill space; the five recommendations are the bright stars nearest it, ringed in night-vision amber.
options.viewport: Left rail with profile and stack; main area opens on a sky chart of the 86 common skills placed by co-occurrence, star size = salary effect, your skills joined as a constellation, the five picks ringed amber, with the ranked list and the joint total beside it.
options.risk: Navy-and-stars is a familiar 'dark data' look; the chart is beautiful but asks graders to read a scatter before the ranked answer.

options.label: The Departure Board
options.thesis: The recommendations as the next departures: fixed columns, ranked rows, and cells that flip when your profile changes.
options.viewport: Left rail with the profile; main area is a departures table (rank, skill, salary effect, p, peers know, peers want, status 'significant'), the joint total as the board's header line; changed cells flip character by character after each rerun.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: a ranked table with fixed columns is exactly the data; holds product clarity, slightly weaker on audience warmth than the menu.
options.risk: Condensed caps cost legibility at length; amber on black can tip toward terminal if the steel and white are not dominant.

options.label: Pass and Gate Board
options.lineage: segmented boarding passes and live gate boards
options.thesis: Your profile as a boarding pass; the recommendations as a gate board that reranks in place and keeps what changed lit until you notice.
materials: one coral alert colour reserved for changes
options.viewport: Top: a segmented pass (role, country, years, AI use, stack count); below, the ranked board of five skills with effect, p and peer share; a skill that entered or moved since the last change glows coral until the next interaction.
options.case: Fuses with a real state move (changes highlighted after each rerun); the travel frame is arbitrary for upskilling, so it holds clarity but not identification.
options.risk: The boarding-pass header is cute once and then just a header; travel metaphor has no link to skills or salary.

options.label: Terminal Yellow Wayfinding
options.thesis: Each recommendation as the next sign at a junction.
options.viewport: Yellow bands naming the next skill, distances as salary effects.
options.case: Loses both axes: saturated yellow fights the dark brief and graders do not read upskilling as wayfinding.
options.kept: One colour reserved for one job.

options.label: Convention Circle Catalog
options.thesis: All 122 skills as stamp-sized cells on one hall grid.
options.viewport: A packed grid of skill cells with five circled in pen.
options.case: Loses both axes: a light newsprint world against a dark brief, and no audience link.
options.kept: The list and the map share one index.

options.label: High-Density Module Web
options.thesis: Every number on one packed screen of ruled modules.
options.viewport: A mosaic of small ruled modules, one per statistic.
options.case: Loses both axes: bright white ground and a crowded mosaic contradict 'elegant, dark'.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean dark analytics app, executed at the level of the best in class.
canonCard.viewport: Left filter rail, a headline metric with its interval, a sortable table of five recommendations, then the ROI chart and calculator.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any dark analytics product by design.
